facts.fact: L.I. 2523, the National Identity Register (Amendment) Regulations 2026, took effect on 9 June 2026 and replaces visual inspection of the Ghana Card with biometric checks by NIA-approved methods, with penalties including loss of access to the NIA verification system (cited from the Ghana News Agency).

GHA.note: Nothing stated on civil register and ID links.
Only a Bank of Ghana fraud-case figure is cited; no payments mandate, licensing or switch role is stated.
Nothing stated on consumer-protection rules for digital finance.

facts.fact: The article says Ghana's Data Protection Commission was created under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) and exists to oversee personal data; it states no appointment or ruling.
The article names the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) as the law under which the Data Protection Commission was created; it states nothing on commencement, regulations or application.

GHA.note: Nothing stated on government payments to people.
The figures given are SIMs linked to Ghana Cards, not a share of the population enrolled.
Nothing stated on ID numbers at birth.
Nothing stated on who operates or owns the ID system.
SIM registration is not a public register keyed on the ID number.
Biometric checks are stated for verification of the card, not for stopping double enrolment; nothing else on the ID system's robustness.
No survey share of adults with an account is given.

facts.fact: The article treats mobile money as in use in Ghana, saying blocking a SIM cuts off mobile money, and citing e-wallets such as MTN MoMo in about 20% of 13,451 financial-sector fraud cases in the Bank of Ghana's 2023 report.

GHA.note: Nothing stated on electronic payment of taxes or fees.
